To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the quality of instruction, as measured by student evaluations, is positively correlated with student learning.

the most important factors affecting student ratings of instruction are (a) student perceptions of the amount and clarity of instruction, (b) student perceptions of instructor caring, (c) student perceptions of student-teacher interpersonal relationships, and (d) student perceptions of course goals and course difficulty.

students learn more when they perceive that their teacher is interested in their learning, that they are able to understand what the teacher is trying to teach them, and that they are motivated to do the things that will help them learn.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evaluation of instruction and not the evaluation of students.
the question, "What are the effects of instruction on student learning and motivation?"
the evaluation of the effectiveness of instruction in terms of the learning that occurs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we need to know more about the processes that are being evaluated.
we know a great deal more about how to evaluate than we currently use, and that there is much more that can be known and that can be done to improve the effectiveness of instructional evaluation.
the current practices of instructional evaluation, as represented in the Marsh article, are sound, but that there is room for improvement.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we know a great deal about the evaluation of instructional effectiveness and that we have a great deal more to learn.
we have learned a great deal about what we should not do, but we have not learned enough about what we should do.
we have a good understanding of how to evaluate the effectiveness of instruction in terms of its impact on student cognitive and academic performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we should be looking at the student's perspective in evaluating instruction.
the evaluation of instruction is not an isolated event.
the current emphasis on cognitive outcomes is not sufficient to evaluate instruction and that the evaluation process should be more student-centered.
